insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for modeled attribution. This protocol settles purchase verification at ~$0.10 per confirmed receipt — a 50–200x cost difference rooted in cryptographic proof, not inference.

With Chrome cookie deprecation complete and fingerprinting increasingly blocked, the industry has no cross-ecosystem, identity-free purchase signal at scale. Verified receipts fill that gap structurally, not as a workaround.

Amazon, Walmart, and every retailer with a loyalty program each see only their own slice of consumer spend. This aggregate captures verified purchases across competing ecosystems simultaneously — a view none of them can buy from each other.

insights.topic: Organic geographic diffusion as adoption signal
insights.insight: 19 active metro and non-metro markets now covered, with rural corridors spanning both coasts and the upper Midwest — none of it attributed to paid acquisition. Burst-quiet-burst diffusion patterns indicate social graph propagation, which is harder to reverse than paid growth.

insights.topic: Category breadth expanding to DTC digital
insights.insight: After 130+ cycles of physical retail only, a Shopify brand entered the verified receipt mix — meaning the signal window now captures online DTC purchases alongside in-store. Category entropy is at its highest recorded level, indicating broader market coverage.

Only 3.3% of verified receipts have been settled via Lightning Network payout, meaning the incentive layer is not yet converting at scale. Brands evaluating this as a data source should weight the receipt volume signal, but note that low claim rates may indicate friction in the user loop that could slow future supply growth.
